summary: Puerto Rico is a classic role-selection economic game where players build plantations and buildings on individual boards, choosing roles each round that give everyone an action but a bonus to the picker. It's a masterclass in efficient engine-building with a distinctive twist: shipped goods and buildings score points, but hoarded doubloons at game end are worthless.
praised: Innovative role-selection mechanism that influenced a generation of euros
Deep strategic tension between building, shipping, and producing
Still holds up as a tight, well-balanced design
criticised: Colonial theme (plantations, colonists) has aged poorly and draws criticism
Can have a long, dry midgame with a lot of downtime between turns
Some role/building combos considered stronger than others in analysis
Player elimination-adjacent feel if you fall behind on production

interaction.kind: role selection and shared shipping/market competition
interaction.detail: Players affect each other mainly by picking roles that deny bonus benefits to others and by competing for limited shipping space and a shared trading house, but the plantations and buildings themselves sit on each player's own board. The colonist supply and ships are the main shared resources creating tension.

scoring.why: Victory points come mainly from buildings and shipped goods, with money serving only as a means to that end.
scoring.how_you_win: You win by converting production and shipping into victory points faster than opponents, since leftover doubloons don't count at the end.
